answer: Sequential scarcity slots. Each identity must occupy a unique slot in a rate-limited inlet: a single admission channel releases new identities only as fast as old ones go dormant past a fixed timeout. A pearl of proof—a recent, unpredictable challenge value emitted by the channel—must be embedded per slot, and slot metadata is immutable, so duplicates get rejected at the ivory ledger check. Cost to an attacker: time, since clones queue behind the drip rate and cannot batch-admit.
